1 # Report Formatting 2 3 ## The one rule 4 5 **A report must not overstate its own coverage.** Every other rule in this file serves that 6 one. The report may print **less** than the scan found — a mistyped marker, a dead agent, a 7 pass that never ran — and when it does it says so in words. It may never claim to print 8 **more**. A report that shows 14 findings and reads as if it showed all of them is the defect 9 this whole design exists to kill. 10 11 ## Who reads this file 12 13 Nothing composes a report from this template any more. There are two readers: 14 15 - **SKILL.md Turn 4 step 5a** — the pass writing its findings into `run-K.md`. It uses the 16 **finding block** shape below: title line, location line, `**Description**`, diff `**Fix**` 17 block. Those bytes are pasted straight through into the report, so they are written in the 18 report's own shape while the pass still has context to spare. 19 - **`references/assemble.sh`** — the assembler. Everything below the finding block — the 20 banner, the Scope table, the ordering, the Findings List, the Leads section, "Known from 21 earlier scans", the disclaimer — is what the assembler emits. 22 23 **This file settles the shape. `report-language.md` settles the words.** Every sentence a 24 human reads in the report — the finding title, the Description, the Lead description, the 25 Lead's code smells — is written in Simplified Technical English, and that file holds the rules. 26 It is read by the same Turn 4 step 5a that writes the block, and it is in all twelve agent 27 bundles. It never reaches the diff in a **Fix** block, the bug-class label inside a key, or an 28 identifier on a location line: those three are data, and it says so. 29 30 **The template is the contract the assembler emits, not a shape a model imitates.** A later 31 editor must not re-teach the orchestrator to write it. The orchestrator under context pressure 32 is the thing that failed; the step that must not lose a finding holds no model judgment. 33 34 ## Report Path 35 36 **Every scan assembles `.solidity-auditor/runs/{stamp}/full-report.md`** — the whole report, 37 banner line down to the disclaimer — at any pass count, with or without flags. That file is 38 the report. There is exactly one producer of it, and it is the assembler. 39 40 `--file-output` makes a **copy** of that file into the current working directory as 41 `{project-name}-pashov-ai-audit-report-{stamp}.md`, where `{project-name}` is the repo root 42 basename and `{stamp}` is `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` at scan time. A copy, not a second build — 43 nothing regenerates, so the flag cannot collapse the report the way the terminal once did. The 44 flag never causes a report to be produced; it only decides whether a copy lands where the 45 runner can see it. 46 47 The `run-K.md` files stay in `.solidity-auditor/runs/{stamp}/` under the same stamp, so a 48 report and the runs that produced it are tied together by eye. They are never copied into the 49 working directory — they are memory, not reports. 50 51 ## Output Format 52 53 This is what the assembler emits. 54 55 ```` 56 # 🔐 Security Review — 57 58 --- 59 60 ## Scope 61 62 | | | 63 | --- | --- | 64 | **Mode** | ALL / default / filename | 65 | **Files reviewed** | `File1.sol` · `File2.sol`
`File3.sol` · `File4.sol` | 66 | **Confidence threshold (1-100)** | N | 67 | **Passes** | 3 | 68 | **Memory** | 12 records before this scan · 14 after · `a1b2c3d` | 69 | **Run files** | ⚠️ 2 findings marked, 1 readable. 1 could not be read. | 70 71 --- 72 73 ## Findings 74 75 [95] **1. ** 76 77 `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 95 · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (4 scans) <!-- runs segment only when passes > 1; memory segment only when memory is on --> 78 79 **Description** 80 <The vulnerable code pattern and why it is exploitable, in 1 short sentence> 81 82 **Fix** 83 84 ```diff 85 - vulnerable line(s) 86 + fixed line(s) 87 ``` 88 89 --- 90 91 [82] **2. <Title>** 92 93 `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 82 94 95 **Description** 96 <The vulnerable code pattern and why it is exploitable, in 1 short sentence> 97 98 **Fix** 99 100 ```diff 101 - vulnerable line(s) 102 + fixed line(s) 103 ``` 104 105 --- 106 107 < ... all above-threshold findings > 108 109 --- 110 111 [60] **3. <Title>** 112 113 `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 60 114 115 **Description** 116 <The vulnerable code pattern and why it is exploitable, in 1 short sentence> 117 118 --- 119 120 < ... all below-threshold findings (description only, no Fix block) > 121 122 --- 123 124 Findings List 125 126 | # | Confidence | Title | 127 |---|---|---| 128 | 1 | [95] | <title> | 129 | 2 | [82] | <title> | 130 | 3 | [75] | <title> | 131 | | | **Below Confidence Threshold** | 132 | 4 | [60] | <title> | 133 134 --- 135 136 ## Leads 137 138 _Vulnerability trails with concrete code smells where the full exploit path could not be completed in one analysis pass. These are not false positives — they are high-signal leads for manual review. Not scored._ 139 140 - **<Title>** — `Contract.function` · NEW — Code smells: <missing guard, unsafe arithmetic, etc.> — <1-2 sentence description of the trail and what remains unverified> <!-- memory segment only when memory is on --> 141 - **<Title>** — `Contract.function` · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (2 scans) — Code smells: <...> — <1-2 sentence description> <!-- runs segment only when passes > 1 --> 142 143 --- 144 145 ## Known from earlier scans 146 147 <!-- only when memory is on AND the ledger held at least one record — see Memory in the report --> 148 149 _Recorded by earlier scans of this repo, not raised again by this one. Not re-checked — a record here may be fixed, or may still be live and missed. `.solidity-auditor/memory.tsv`._ 150 151 | Scans | Kind | Location | Title | 152 |---|---|---|---| 153 | 4 | FINDING | `Router.swap` | Swap trusts a spot price as an oracle | 154 | 2 | LEAD | `Vault.sweep` | Sweep lets the owner take user deposits | 155 156 --- 157 158 > ⚠️ This review was performed by an AI assistant. AI analysis can never verify the complete absence of vulnerabilities and no guarantee of security is given. Team security reviews, bug bounty programs, and on-chain monitoring are strongly recommended. For a consultation regarding your projects' security, visit [https://www.pashov.com](https://www.pashov.com) 159 160 ```` 161 162 **Rules describing the output**, all of them held by the assembler and none of them addressed 163 to a model: 164 165 - Findings are sorted by confidence, highest first. 166 - A finding at or above the threshold carries a **Description** and a diff **Fix** block. One 167 below carries the **Description** only. Nothing in the run file marks which side of the line 168 a finding sits on — it is re-derived from the confidence, so there is one source of truth. 169 - The **Below Confidence Threshold** separator row is printed whenever at least one finding 170 falls below the threshold, and left out when none does. Without it the table runs 1, 2, 3 171 with nothing to mark the boundary, so a reader of the table alone cannot tell which findings 172 carry no **Fix** block. 173 - **Empty cases say so in words, never with an empty table**: `_None — this scan raised no 174 findings._` in place of the Findings List, `_None._` under Leads, `**Body missing** — pass K 175 raised this finding and wrote no description.` in place of a body. 176 - **A `Run files` row appears only when the structure check disagrees.** The model types the 177 markers that bound each finding in a run file, so it can mistype one. The assembler counts 178 open markers against close markers against readable blocks, and prints the disagreement as a 179 Scope row naming how many findings could not be read. Everything readable is still printed 180 and the assembler never stops. That row is the one rule at the top made mechanical. 181 - **The Scope table's column padding is not part of the shape.** Markdown renders 182 `| **Mode** | default |` and a space-padded form identically, and the padding above is for 183 reading this file. Content and order are the contract; character widths are not. 184 185 **The threshold is 75**, set in `judging.md` and printed in the Scope row above. It is named 186 in `judging.md` and nowhere else; this file reads it from there. A finding at 75 or above gets 187 a description and a **Fix** block, one below 75 gets the description only. A promoted lead 188 lands at exactly 75, so it clears — that is why the number is 75. 189 190 ## The size trigger 191 192 **More than 20 findings.** At 20 the terminal prints the assembled file word for word; at 21 193 it stops printing findings. Findings only — above and below the threshold together. **Leads 194 are excluded from the trigger count**, so a scan with 18 findings and 40 leads prints in full. 195 196 The trigger is on **size, not on flags**. A plain scan of a small contract is unchanged; a 197 plain scan of a big one gets the new shape. 198 199 **Above the trigger the terminal prints four things:** the banner, the Scope table unchanged, 200 a **Findings List holding the top 3 findings**, and the path to the full report — then the 201 disclaimer. About fifteen lines. 202 203 The full report is unaffected. Above the trigger, as below it, `full-report.md` holds every 204 finding in the shape above — only the terminal changes. 205 206 **The slice is honest because it is counted.** The table's header reads 207 `Findings List — top 3 of {F}`, and that `{F}` is the whole rule: 208 209 - **A report may print less than the scan found. It may never look like it printed more.** 210 A bare list of three findings breaks that — a reader cannot tell a truncated list from a 211 complete one. `top 3 of 52` cannot be misread. 212 - **The total goes in the header, not a footnote.** A reader who sees the table sees the 213 total in the same glance. This is not a style choice; a footnote can be scrolled past. 214 - **Three rows, and nothing else is enumerated.** No Leads, no "Known from earlier scans", 215 no findings past the third. 216 217 > **This replaces the older "nothing is enumerated above the trigger" rule**, which forbade 218 > every top-N slice. That rule was right that bare truncation lies and wrong to conclude no 219 > slice can be honest; a counted one is. A later editor must not restore the blanket ban by 220 > citing the half of the argument that survived. 221 222 **The rows are extracted by shell, never typed.** One `awk` over the assembled file — which is 223 already sorted highest-confidence first, so no sort happens in the terminal step. The 224 orchestrator has read dozens of findings by then and is the least reliable thing in the room; 225 the extractor cannot mis-rank, mis-quote a function name or invent a confidence. The command 226 is in `dedup-and-assembly.md` Turn 5 step 3b. 227 228 **The `Seen` column appears only when the `Passes` row does** — that is, when the pass count is 229 above 1. A plain scan's location line carries no `seen in k/N runs`, so the column is dropped 230 from the header, the separator and the rows together. A five-column header over four-column 231 rows draws as a broken table. 232 233 **There is no counts summary.** The `{F} findings, {L} leads` line and the 234 `100-90 / 89-75 / below 75` split are not printed. `top 3 of {F}` carries the only total the 235 moment needs, and the bucket split stood between the reader and the path. The buckets are still 236 **computed** as a self-check — `A + B + C` must equal `F`, in every mode, or the assembled file 237 is malformed and the scan says so instead of printing a slice of it. 238 239 The path line names `.solidity-auditor/runs/{stamp}/full-report.md`, or — when `--file-output` 240 was passed — the **copy** and only the copy. Never both: two paths to identical bytes answer a 241 question the runner did not ask at the moment they want one filename. That line is the only 242 part of the block a flag changes. 243 244 The exact wording, spacing and order of the block are in `dedup-and-assembly.md` Turn 5 step 245 3b, which is where the terminal is printed. 246 247 ## The freeze 248 249 **A small scan with no flags prints what it printed before any of this existed.** Below the 250 trigger the terminal prints `full-report.md` word for word — every byte, nothing added, 251 nothing cut, no preface — so the freeze is a property of the assembled file. 252 253 The freeze is a **diff against `golden/plain-full-report.md`**, the frozen plain-path report, 254 and it covers the report's **content and order, not its column padding** and not what lands on 255 disk. Byte-identity against "today" was tried and is unmeetable: no captured report exists 256 anywhere, and today's bytes were composed by a model from a template that contradicted itself. 257 The golden file is what replaced it. 258 259 What the freeze does **not** cover: writing files. Every scan now writes a runs directory and 260 assembles a report there, at any pass count. Writing a file is not printing, and the freeze is 261 on printed output. 262 263 ## Memory in the report 264 265 Everything in this section is printed **only when memory is on** (`--memory`, or a pass count 266 above 1). With memory off the assembled file carries no extra rows, no extra segments, no 267 extra sections and no dangling `·`, and below the trigger it still diffs clean against the 268 golden file. 269 270 **Segment order on the meta line.** One dot-separated chain, in a fixed order: 271 272 ``` 273 `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 95 · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (4 scans) 274 ``` 275 276 location · confidence · runs · memory. **A segment appears only when it carries information** — 277 `seen in k/N runs` needs more than one run, `KNOWN (n scans)` / `NEW` needs memory on. So: 278 279 | Scan | Meta line | 280 |---|---| 281 | 1 pass, no flags | `` `Vault.withdraw` · Confidence: 95 `` | 282 | 1 pass, `--memory` | `` … · Confidence: 95 · KNOWN (4 scans) `` | 283 | 3 passes | `` … · Confidence: 95 · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (4 scans) `` | 284 285 `KNOWN (4 scans)` and `NEW` are the ledger's own two words, so the report and the file say the 286 same thing. **`n` counts this scan.** The tag is derived by the assembler from 287 `memory-before.tsv` — the pre-scan photocopy — and `n` is that row's `scans` **plus one**: the 288 scan that is printing has just found it again, and the ledger already holds that same number. 289 Printing the stored count instead would show a report one behind its own ledger. `NEW` carries 290 no count. The tag is **not** carried in the run-file marker: one source, so the report and the 291 ledger cannot disagree. 292 293 The `Scans` column of "Known from earlier scans" is the opposite case and is printed **as 294 stored**: this scan did not raise those records, so nothing about them counts up. The 295 **Findings List** table is unchanged — it stays `# | Confidence | Title`. 296 297 Leads carry the same segments as findings, on their own line, because a Lead is a full ledger 298 record. 299 300 **The `Memory` row in Scope.** `<records in the ledger before this scan> records before this 301 scan · <records after the merge> after · `<sha>``. The SHA is the one every row of this scan 302 wrote; `none` when the repo has no commits. # Report Formatting ## The one rule **A report must not overstate its own coverage.** Every other rule in this file serves that one. The report may print **less** than the scan found — a mistyped marker, a dead agent, a pass that never ran — and when it does it says so in words. It may never claim to print **more**. A report that shows 14 findings and reads as if it showed all of them is the defect this whole design exists to kill. ## Who reads this file Nothing composes a report from this template any more. There are two readers: - **SKILL.md Turn 4 step 5a** — the pass writing its findings into `run-K.md`. It uses the **finding block** shape below: title line, location line, `**Description**`, diff `**Fix**` block. Those bytes are pasted straight through into the report, so they are written in the report's own shape while the pass still has context to spare. - **`references/assemble.sh`** — the assembler. Everything below the finding block — the banner, the Scope table, the ordering, the Findings List, the Leads section, "Known from earlier scans", the disclaimer — is what the assembler emits. **This file settles the shape. `report-language.md` settles the words.** Every sentence a human reads in the report — the finding title, the Description, the Lead description, the Lead's code smells — is written in Simplified Technical English, and that file holds the rules. It is read by the same Turn 4 step 5a that writes the block, and it is in all twelve agent bundles. It never reaches the diff in a **Fix** block, the bug-class label inside a key, or an identifier on a location line: those three are data, and it says so. **The template is the contract the assembler emits, not a shape a model imitates.** A later editor must not re-teach the orchestrator to write it. The orchestrator under context pressure is the thing that failed; the step that must not lose a finding holds no model judgment. ## Report Path **Every scan assembles `.solidity-auditor/runs/{stamp}/full-report.md`** — the whole report, banner line down to the disclaimer — at any pass count, with or without flags. That file is the report. There is exactly one producer of it, and it is the assembler. `--file-output` makes a **copy** of that file into the current working directory as `{project-name}-pashov-ai-audit-report-{stamp}.md`, where `{project-name}` is the repo root basename and `{stamp}` is `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` at scan time. A copy, not a second build — nothing regenerates, so the flag cannot collapse the report the way the terminal once did. The flag never causes a report to be produced; it only decides whether a copy lands where the runner can see it. The `run-K.md` files stay in `.solidity-auditor/runs/{stamp}/` under the same stamp, so a report and the runs that produced it are tied together by eye. They are never copied into the working directory — they are memory, not reports. ## Output Format This is what the assembler emits. ```` # 🔐 Security Review — --- ## Scope | | | | --- | --- | | **Mode** | ALL / default / filename | | **Files reviewed** | `File1.sol` · `File2.sol`
`File3.sol` · `File4.sol` | | **Confidence threshold (1-100)** | N | | **Passes** | 3 | | **Memory** | 12 records before this scan · 14 after · `a1b2c3d` | | **Run files** | ⚠️ 2 findings marked, 1 readable. 1 could not be read. | --- ## Findings [95] **1. ** `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 95 · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (4 scans) <!-- runs segment only when passes > 1; memory segment only when memory is on --> **Description** <The vulnerable code pattern and why it is exploitable, in 1 short sentence> **Fix** ```diff - vulnerable line(s) + fixed line(s) ``` --- [82] **2. <Title>** `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 82 **Description** <The vulnerable code pattern and why it is exploitable, in 1 short sentence> **Fix** ```diff - vulnerable line(s) + fixed line(s) ``` --- < ... all above-threshold findings > --- [60] **3. <Title>** `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 60 **Description** <The vulnerable code pattern and why it is exploitable, in 1 short sentence> --- < ... all below-threshold findings (description only, no Fix block) > --- Findings List | # | Confidence | Title | |---|---|---| | 1 | [95] | <title> | | 2 | [82] | <title> | | 3 | [75] | <title> | | | | **Below Confidence Threshold** | | 4 | [60] | <title> | --- ## Leads _Vulnerability trails with concrete code smells where the full exploit path could not be completed in one analysis pass. These are not false positives — they are high-signal leads for manual review. Not scored._ - **<Title>** — `Contract.function` · NEW — Code smells: <missing guard, unsafe arithmetic, etc.> — <1-2 sentence description of the trail and what remains unverified> <!-- memory segment only when memory is on --> - **<Title>** — `Contract.function` · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (2 scans) — Code smells: <...> — <1-2 sentence description> <!-- runs segment only when passes > 1 --> --- ## Known from earlier scans <!-- only when memory is on AND the ledger held at least one record — see Memory in the report --> _Recorded by earlier scans of this repo, not raised again by this one. Not re-checked — a record here may be fixed, or may still be live and missed. `.solidity-auditor/memory.tsv`._ | Scans | Kind | Location | Title | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | FINDING | `Router.swap` | Swap trusts a spot price as an oracle | | 2 | LEAD | `Vault.sweep` | Sweep lets the owner take user deposits | --- > ⚠️ This review was performed by an AI assistant. AI analysis can never verify the complete absence of vulnerabilities and no guarantee of security is given. Team security reviews, bug bounty programs, and on-chain monitoring are strongly recommended. For a consultation regarding your projects' security, visit [https://www.pashov.com](https://www.pashov.com) ```` **Rules describing the output**, all of them held by the assembler and none of them addressed to a model: - Findings are sorted by confidence, highest first. - A finding at or above the threshold carries a **Description** and a diff **Fix** block. One below carries the **Description** only. Nothing in the run file marks which side of the line a finding sits on — it is re-derived from the confidence, so there is one source of truth. - The **Below Confidence Threshold** separator row is printed whenever at least one finding falls below the threshold, and left out when none does. Without it the table runs 1, 2, 3 with nothing to mark the boundary, so a reader of the table alone cannot tell which findings carry no **Fix** block. - **Empty cases say so in words, never with an empty table**: `_None — this scan raised no findings._` in place of the Findings List, `_None._` under Leads, `**Body missing** — pass K raised this finding and wrote no description.` in place of a body. - **A `Run files` row appears only when the structure check disagrees.** The model types the markers that bound each finding in a run file, so it can mistype one. The assembler counts open markers against close markers against readable blocks, and prints the disagreement as a Scope row naming how many findings could not be read. Everything readable is still printed and the assembler never stops. That row is the one rule at the top made mechanical. - **The Scope table's column padding is not part of the shape.** Markdown renders `| **Mode** | default |` and a space-padded form identically, and the padding above is for reading this file. Content and order are the contract; character widths are not. **The threshold is 75**, set in `judging.md` and printed in the Scope row above. It is named in `judging.md` and nowhere else; this file reads it from there. A finding at 75 or above gets a description and a **Fix** block, one below 75 gets the description only. A promoted lead lands at exactly 75, so it clears — that is why the number is 75. ## The size trigger **More than 20 findings.** At 20 the terminal prints the assembled file word for word; at 21 it stops printing findings. Findings only — above and below the threshold together. **Leads are excluded from the trigger count**, so a scan with 18 findings and 40 leads prints in full. The trigger is on **size, not on flags**. A plain scan of a small contract is unchanged; a plain scan of a big one gets the new shape. **Above the trigger the terminal prints four things:** the banner, the Scope table unchanged, a **Findings List holding the top 3 findings**, and the path to the full report — then the disclaimer. About fifteen lines. The full report is unaffected. Above the trigger, as below it, `full-report.md` holds every finding in the shape above — only the terminal changes. **The slice is honest because it is counted.** The table's header reads `Findings List — top 3 of {F}`, and that `{F}` is the whole rule: - **A report may print less than the scan found. It may never look like it printed more.** A bare list of three findings breaks that — a reader cannot tell a truncated list from a complete one. `top 3 of 52` cannot be misread. - **The total goes in the header, not a footnote.** A reader who sees the table sees the total in the same glance. This is not a style choice; a footnote can be scrolled past. - **Three rows, and nothing else is enumerated.** No Leads, no "Known from earlier scans", no findings past the third. > **This replaces the older "nothing is enumerated above the trigger" rule**, which forbade > every top-N slice. That rule was right that bare truncation lies and wrong to conclude no > slice can be honest; a counted one is. A later editor must not restore the blanket ban by > citing the half of the argument that survived. **The rows are extracted by shell, never typed.** One `awk` over the assembled file — which is already sorted highest-confidence first, so no sort happens in the terminal step. The orchestrator has read dozens of findings by then and is the least reliable thing in the room; the extractor cannot mis-rank, mis-quote a function name or invent a confidence. The command is in `dedup-and-assembly.md` Turn 5 step 3b. **The `Seen` column appears only when the `Passes` row does** — that is, when the pass count is above 1. A plain scan's location line carries no `seen in k/N runs`, so the column is dropped from the header, the separator and the rows together. A five-column header over four-column rows draws as a broken table. **There is no counts summary.** The `{F} findings, {L} leads` line and the `100-90 / 89-75 / below 75` split are not printed. `top 3 of {F}` carries the only total the moment needs, and the bucket split stood between the reader and the path. The buckets are still **computed** as a self-check — `A + B + C` must equal `F`, in every mode, or the assembled file is malformed and the scan says so instead of printing a slice of it. The path line names `.solidity-auditor/runs/{stamp}/full-report.md`, or — when `--file-output` was passed — the **copy** and only the copy. Never both: two paths to identical bytes answer a question the runner did not ask at the moment they want one filename. That line is the only part of the block a flag changes. The exact wording, spacing and order of the block are in `dedup-and-assembly.md` Turn 5 step 3b, which is where the terminal is printed. ## The freeze **A small scan with no flags prints what it printed before any of this existed.** Below the trigger the terminal prints `full-report.md` word for word — every byte, nothing added, nothing cut, no preface — so the freeze is a property of the assembled file. The freeze is a **diff against `golden/plain-full-report.md`**, the frozen plain-path report, and it covers the report's **content and order, not its column padding** and not what lands on disk. Byte-identity against "today" was tried and is unmeetable: no captured report exists anywhere, and today's bytes were composed by a model from a template that contradicted itself. The golden file is what replaced it. What the freeze does **not** cover: writing files. Every scan now writes a runs directory and assembles a report there, at any pass count. Writing a file is not printing, and the freeze is on printed output. ## Memory in the report Everything in this section is printed **only when memory is on** (`--memory`, or a pass count above 1). With memory off the assembled file carries no extra rows, no extra segments, no extra sections and no dangling `·`, and below the trigger it still diffs clean against the golden file. **Segment order on the meta line.** One dot-separated chain, in a fixed order: ``` `ContractName.functionName` · Confidence: 95 · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (4 scans) ``` location · confidence · runs · memory. **A segment appears only when it carries information** — `seen in k/N runs` needs more than one run, `KNOWN (n scans)` / `NEW` needs memory on. So: | Scan | Meta line | |---|---| | 1 pass, no flags | `` `Vault.withdraw` · Confidence: 95 `` | | 1 pass, `--memory` | `` … · Confidence: 95 · KNOWN (4 scans) `` | | 3 passes | `` … · Confidence: 95 · seen in 2/3 runs · KNOWN (4 scans) `` | `KNOWN (4 scans)` and `NEW` are the ledger's own two words, so the report and the file say the same thing. **`n` counts this scan.** The tag is derived by the assembler from `memory-before.tsv` — the pre-scan photocopy — and `n` is that row's `scans` **plus one**: the scan that is printing has just found it again, and the ledger already holds that same number. Printing the stored count instead would show a report one behind its own ledger. `NEW` carries no count. The tag is **not** carried in the run-file marker: one source, so the report and the ledger cannot disagree. 1	# Finding Validation
2	
3	Every finding passes four sequential gates. Fail any gate → **rejected** or **demoted** to lead. Later gates are not evaluated for failed findings.
4	
5	You are not defending the code. The job of these gates is to verify the attacker's claimed exploit actually fires end-to-end — anything that interrupts the attack between the attacker's call and the harm means the agent's claim does not execute, and only then does it fail to qualify as a finding.
6	
7	## Gate 1 — Attack execution
8	
9	Trace the agent's claimed attack path from caller to harm. Read every guard, check, modifier, and constraint that sits on that path. Confirm that none of them interrupts the attack before the exploit step fires.
10	- A specific guard / check / modifier on the attack path interrupts the claimed exploit step before harm occurs (quote the exact line and trace it) → **REJECTED** (or **DEMOTE** if a related code smell remains)
11	- The supposed interruption is speculative ("probably wouldn't happen", "the caller would notice", "the deployer would set X") → **clears**, continue
12	
13	## Gate 2 — Reachability
14	
15	Prove the vulnerable state exists in a live deployment.
16	
17	- Structurally impossible (enforced invariant prevents it) → **REJECTED**
18	- Requires privileged actions outside normal operation → **DEMOTE**
19	- Achievable through normal usage or common token behaviors → **clears**, continue
20	
21	## Gate 3 — Trigger
22	
23	Prove an unprivileged actor executes the attack.
24	
25	- Only trusted roles can trigger → **DEMOTE**
26	- Unprivileged actor triggers profitably → **clears**, continue
27	
28	**Admin-action findings — reject unless an unprivileged amplifier is named.** This applies ONLY to actions performed by admin/owner, NOT to unprivileged attacker actions. If the harm requires the admin acting maliciously or against documented intent, **REJECT** — do not even emit as a LEAD (stricter than the DEMOTE above). The finding clears only when the body names a concrete unprivileged amplifier:
29	
30	- **race** — admin sets X mid-flow; an unprivileged user exploits the window before the update propagates.
31	- **retroactive sweep** — an admin update rewrites a pending value already credited.
32	- **asymmetric formula** — admin output chains into a formula an unprivileged actor profits from.
33	- **access gap** — missing guard, tautological auth, or missing init guard (the access mechanism itself is the bug).
34	
35	No amplifier named → **REJECTED**. Amplifier named → judge it on that unprivileged path.
36	
37	## Gate 4 — Impact
38	
39	Prove material harm to an identifiable victim.
40	
41	- Self-harm only → **REJECTED**
42	- Dust-level, no compounding → **DEMOTE**
43	- Material loss to identifiable victim → **CONFIRMED**
44	
45	## Confidence
46	
47	Start at **100**, deduct: partial attack path **-20**, bounded non-compounding impact **-15**, requires specific (but achievable) state **-10**. Confidence ≥ 75 gets description + fix. Below 75 gets description only.
48	
49	**The threshold is 75, and it is set here.** `report-formatting.md` reads it from this line and states it nowhere else. It is 75 and not 80 because the three lead-promotion rules below all land a promoted lead at exactly 75: at a threshold of 80 every cross-contract echo, every multi-agent convergence and every completed partial path would be promoted to a finding and then printed with no **Fix** block. Moving this number means moving those three, or the promotions stop being worth making.
50	
51	## Safe patterns (do not flag)
52	
53	- `unchecked` in 0.8+ (but verify the reasoning is correct)
54	- Explicit narrowing casts in 0.8+ (reverts on overflow)
55	- MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY burn on first deposit
56	- SafeERC20 (`safeTransfer`/`safeTransferFrom`)
57	- `nonReentrant` (only flag cross-contract attacks)
58	- Two-step admin transfer
59	- Consistent protocol-favoring rounding unless compounding or zero-rounding
60	
61	## Lead promotion
62	
63	Before finalizing leads, promote where warranted:
64	
65	- **Cross-contract echo.** Same root cause confirmed as FINDING in one contract → promote in every contract where the identical pattern appears.
66	- **Multi-agent convergence.** 2+ agents flagged same area, lead was demoted (not rejected) → promote to FINDING at confidence 75.
67	- **Partial-path completion.** Only weakness is incomplete trace but path is reachable and unguarded → promote to FINDING at confidence 75, **description only — a deliberate exception to the threshold**. 75 clears the line, so this finding would otherwise carry a **Fix** block; it does not, because the trace it would fix was never completed. The other two promotions above take their **Fix** block normally.
68	
69	## Leads
70	
71	High-signal trails for manual investigation. No confidence score, no fix — title, code smells, and what remains unverified.
72	
73	## Do Not Report
74	
75	Linter/compiler issues, gas micro-opts, naming, NatSpec. Admin privileges by design. Missing events. Centralization without exploit path. Implausible preconditions (but fee-on-transfer, rebasing, blacklisting ARE plausible for contracts accepting arbitrary tokens).
76

## Gate 2 — Reachability

Prove the vulnerable state exists in a live deployment.

- Structurally impossible (enforced invariant prevents it) → **REJECTED**
- Requires privileged actions outside normal operation → **DEMOTE**
- Achievable through normal usage or common token behaviors → **clears**, continue

## Gate 3 — Trigger

Prove an unprivileged actor executes the attack.

- Only trusted roles can trigger → **DEMOTE**
- Unprivileged actor triggers profitably → **clears**, continue

**Admin-action findings — reject unless an unprivileged amplifier is named.** This applies ONLY to actions performed by admin/owner, NOT to unprivileged attacker actions. If the harm requires the admin acting maliciously or against documented intent, **REJECT** — do not even emit as a LEAD (stricter than the DEMOTE above). The finding clears only when the body names a concrete unprivileged amplifier:

- **race** — admin sets X mid-flow; an unprivileged user exploits the window before the update propagates.
- **retroactive sweep** — an admin update rewrites a pending value already credited.
- **asymmetric formula** — admin output chains into a formula an unprivileged actor profits from.
- **access gap** — missing guard, tautological auth, or missing init guard (the access mechanism itself is the bug).

No amplifier named → **REJECTED**. Amplifier named → judge it on that unprivileged path.

## Gate 4 — Impact

Prove material harm to an identifiable victim.

- Self-harm only → **REJECTED**
- Dust-level, no compounding → **DEMOTE**
- Material loss to identifiable victim → **CONFIRMED**

## Confidence

Start at **100**, deduct: partial attack path **-20**, bounded non-compounding impact **-15**, requires specific (but achievable) state **-10**. Confidence ≥ 75 gets description + fix. Below 75 gets description only.

**The threshold is 75, and it is set here.** `report-formatting.md` reads it from this line and states it nowhere else. It is 75 and not 80 because the three lead-promotion rules below all land a promoted lead at exactly 75: at a threshold of 80 every cross-contract echo, every multi-agent convergence and every completed partial path would be promoted to a finding and then printed with no **Fix** block. Moving this number means moving those three, or the promotions stop being worth making.

## Safe patterns (do not flag)

- `unchecked` in 0.8+ (but verify the reasoning is correct)
- Explicit narrowing casts in 0.8+ (reverts on overflow)
- MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY burn on first deposit
- SafeERC20 (`safeTransfer`/`safeTransferFrom`)
- `nonReentrant` (only flag cross-contract attacks)
- Two-step admin transfer
- Consistent protocol-favoring rounding unless compounding or zero-rounding

## Lead promotion

Before finalizing leads, promote where warranted:

- **Cross-contract echo.** Same root cause confirmed as FINDING in one contract → promote in every contract where the identical pattern appears.
- **Multi-agent convergence.** 2+ agents flagged same area, lead was demoted (not rejected) → promote to FINDING at confidence 75.
- **Partial-path completion.** Only weakness is incomplete trace but path is reachable and unguarded → promote to FINDING at confidence 75, **description only — a deliberate exception to the threshold**. 75 clears the line, so this finding would otherwise carry a **Fix** block; it does not, because the trace it would fix was never completed. The other two promotions above take their **Fix** block normally.

## Leads

High-signal trails for manual investigation. No confidence score, no fix — title, code smells, and what remains unverified.

## Do Not Report

Linter/compiler issues, gas micro-opts, naming, NatSpec. Admin privileges by design. Missing events. Centralization without exploit path. Implausible preconditions (but fee-on-transfer, rebasing, blacklisting ARE plausible for contracts accepting arbitrary tokens).

67	    the effect: `the caller keeps the tokens and the pool keeps the debt`.

69	    not present`.

71	    balance, so an attacker who moves the balance moves the price.`

73	    defect or its effect. `Swap trusts a spot price as an oracle.`
74	    Not `Oracle manipulation vulnerability in swap functionality`.

77

79	
80	| Do not write | Write |
81	| --- | --- |
82	| burns the funds | sends the tokens to an address that cannot spend them |
83	| bricks the contract | makes the function fail for every caller, forever |
84	| rug / rugpull | the owner takes the user deposits |
85	| griefing | an attacker makes the function fail for other users |
86	| footgun | (delete the word and name the defect) |
87	| silently swallows the error | ignores the error |
88	| DoS / denial of service | blocks every caller |
89	| attack surface / attack vector | path |
90	| malicious actor / bad actor | an attacker |
91	| leverages / utilizes | uses |
92	| is able to | can |
93	| in order to | to |
94	| arbitrary value | any value the caller chooses |
95	| stale price | old price |
96	| sanity check | check |
97	| happy path | the normal path |
98	| atomically | in one transaction |
99	| trustlessly / permissionlessly | (delete, or name who may call) |
100	| non-zero | more than zero |
101	| cascading failures | (name each failure) |
102	| exponentially / trivially / catastrophically | (delete) |
103	| edge case | (name the input or the state) |
104	
105	## Technical names stay
106	
107	STE-100 keeps technical names, and a security report cannot work without them:
108	`reentrancy`, `slippage`, `oracle`, `revert`, `overflow`, `rounding`, `allowance`, `nonce`,
109	`slot`, `delegatecall`. Use them. They are precise and the reader who fixes Solidity knows
110	them.
111	
112	The rule is what goes **around** them: name the mechanism once with its technical name, then
113	say in plain words what the attacker gets.
114	
115	- No: `Classic CEI violation enabling reentrant drainage of the vault.`
116	- Yes: `The function sends ETH before it lowers the balance, so a reentrant call withdraws
117	  the same deposit twice.`
118	
119	## Worked examples
120	
121	Before, and after. The code the sentence describes did not change.
122	
123	**One**
124	
125	- Before: `Improper validation of the abort address results in a catastrophic loss of user
126	  funds via burning to the zero address.`
127	- After: `The function accepts a zero abort address, so a failed transfer sends the tokens to
128	  an address that nobody controls.`
129	
130	**Two**
131	
132	- Before: `Lack of slippage protection in the swap path exposes users to sandwich attacks,
133	  potentially leading to significant value extraction by MEV searchers.`
134	- After: `The swap sets the minimum output to zero, so an attacker who trades before and
135	  after the victim keeps most of the output.`
136	
137	**Three — a Lead**
138	
139	- Before: `Potential accounting inconsistency stemming from asymmetric fee handling on
140	  deposit/withdraw flows warranting further investigation.`
141	- After: `The deposit takes the fee from the amount, and the withdrawal takes it from the
142	  balance. We did not find the input that makes the two disagree.`
143	
144	## Self-check before you write the block
145	
146	Four questions. Any `no` means rewrite the sentence, not the code:
147	
148	- Does the sentence name **who** acts and **what** they get?
149	- Is it one sentence, twenty-five words or fewer, with no `-ing` clause?
150	- Is every word in it a word the reader does not have to translate?
151	- Are the identifiers, the label and the diff exactly as the source and the agent wrote them?

## Technical names stay

STE-100 keeps technical names, and a security report cannot work without them:
`reentrancy`, `slippage`, `oracle`, `revert`, `overflow`, `rounding`, `allowance`, `nonce`,
`slot`, `delegatecall`. Use them. They are precise and the reader who fixes Solidity knows
them.

The rule is what goes **around** them: name the mechanism once with its technical name, then
say in plain words what the attacker gets.

- No: `Classic CEI violation enabling reentrant drainage of the vault.`
- Yes: `The function sends ETH before it lowers the balance, so a reentrant call withdraws
  the same deposit twice.`

## Worked examples

Before, and after. The code the sentence describes did not change.

**One**

- Before: `Improper validation of the abort address results in a catastrophic loss of user
  funds via burning to the zero address.`
- After: `The function accepts a zero abort address, so a failed transfer sends the tokens to
  an address that nobody controls.`

**Two**

- Before: `Lack of slippage protection in the swap path exposes users to sandwich attacks,
  potentially leading to significant value extraction by MEV searchers.`
- After: `The swap sets the minimum output to zero, so an attacker who trades before and
  after the victim keeps most of the output.`

**Three — a Lead**

- Before: `Potential accounting inconsistency stemming from asymmetric fee handling on
  deposit/withdraw flows warranting further investigation.`
- After: `The deposit takes the fee from the amount, and the withdrawal takes it from the
  balance. We did not find the input that makes the two disagree.`

## Self-check before you write the block

Four questions. Any `no` means rewrite the sentence, not the code:

- Does the sentence name **who** acts and **what** they get?
- Is it one sentence, twenty-five words or fewer, with no `-ing` clause?
- Is every word in it a word the reader does not have to translate?
- Are the identifiers, the label and the diff exactly as the source and the agent wrote them?

# Clean design specification
Ethereum NFT raffle; immutable factory, ERC-1167 clones with immutable implementation. One entry costs 1,000,000 units of canonical six-decimal USDC. One purchase mints a transferable ERC721 ticket representing a contiguous inclusive range. Exactly one ERC721 prize is escrowed atomically at creation. Reserve met awards NFT and 95% sponsor / 5% treasury. Reserve missed awards 80% gross to winner, 15% sponsor, 5% treasury. Refund outcome pays 100% per entry and returns prize. Rounding is floor on aggregate protocol fee; remainder must be allocated without loss. No administrator, mutable configuration or upgrade. Request window [sale end, end+2days); callback accepted strictly before request timestamp+2days. Refunds open at deadline. Callback records result only. Settlement is permissionless, storage-only; redemption requires current ticket owner, burns claim atomically, and must revert all effects on delivery failure. Sponsor and treasury can claim independently after settlement. Never move assets between raffle clones. Quote token and Chainlink wrapper are trusted canonical dependencies; arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted. Frontend discovery is advisory; transaction decisions must reread current chain state.

This specification was composed before scanner results and historical findings. Source, not design prose, determines actual behavior. No tests, audit history, accepted-risk lists or scanner results are provided.

1	// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
2	pragma solidity 0.8.36;
3	
4	import { IVRFV2PlusWrapper } from "@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/vrf/dev/interfaces/IVRFV2PlusWrapper.sol";
5	import { IERC20 } from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol";
6	import { IERC721 } from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC721/IERC721.sol";
7	
8	/// @title raffle.fun Raffle Interface
9	/// @author heesho
10	/// @notice Defines one autonomous NFT raffle using fixed-price USDC entries and one transferable ERC-721 ticket per
11	///         purchase.
12	/// @dev Ticket IDs are sequential. Each ticket stores one inclusive uint128 entry range and remains a transferable
13	///      bearer claim until its owner atomically burns it for redemption or refund. The immutable quote token is trusted
14	///      canonical six-decimal USDC with standard, non-rebasing, fee-free transfers. Supported prizes are honest,
15	///      standards-compliant ERC-721s.
16	/// @custom:version 1.0.0
17	interface IRaffle {
18	    // Types
19	
20	    /// @notice The single authoritative raffle lifecycle and economic result.
21	    enum Status {
22	        /// @notice The clone is initialized and waiting for the factory to escrow the configured prize.
23	        AwaitingPrize,
24	        /// @notice The prize is escrowed and entry sales or post-sale draw initiation are available.
25	        Active,
26	        /// @notice A Chainlink VRF request was accepted and its callback window is open.
27	        Drawing,
28	        /// @notice The reserve was met and the winning ticket may redeem the prize NFT.
29	        NftWon,
30	        /// @notice The reserve was missed and the winning ticket may redeem its cash allocation.
31	        CashWon,
32	        /// @notice Full ticket refunds are enabled and the sponsor may recover the prize NFT.
33	        Refunding
34	    }
35	
36	    /// @notice Complete clone-specific configuration supplied once by the canonical factory.
37	    /// @param sponsor Prize depositor and empty-raffle cancellation authority.
38	    /// @param sponsorRecipient Immutable recipient of sponsor quote proceeds and any returned prize.
39	    /// @param protocolTreasury Immutable recipient of protocol fees.
40	    /// @param prizeToken Standards-compliant ERC-721 prize contract.
41	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID of the prize escrowed by this raffle.
42	    /// @param raffleId One-based canonical factory identifier for this raffle.
43	    /// @param reserveEntries Global raw entry-count threshold selecting the NFT outcome when met or exceeded.
44	    /// @param endTime Unix timestamp, in seconds, at which entry sales end exclusively.
45	    struct RaffleInitParams {
46	        address sponsor;
47	        address sponsorRecipient;
48	        address protocolTreasury;
49	        address prizeToken;
50	        uint256 prizeTokenId;
51	        uint256 raffleId;
52	        uint128 reserveEntries;
53	        uint64 endTime;
54	    }
55	
56	    // Events
57	
58	    /// @notice Emitted when the factory deposits the configured prize and activates the raffle.
59	    /// @param prizeToken ERC-721 contract of the deposited prize.
60	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID of the deposited prize.
61	    /// @param sponsor Address that deposited the prize through the factory.
62	    event PrizeDeposited(address indexed prizeToken, uint256 indexed prizeTokenId, address indexed sponsor);
63	
64	    /// @notice Emitted when a buyer pays for entries and one range ticket is minted.
65	    /// @param buyer Address that paid the six-decimal quote-token amount.
66	    /// @param recipient Address that received the newly minted ticket.
67	    /// @param ticketId Sequential ticket ID assigned to the purchase.
68	    /// @param firstEntry First global raffle entry represented by the ticket, inclusive.
69	    /// @param lastEntry Last global raffle entry represented by the ticket, inclusive.
70	    /// @param entryCount Number of entries represented by the ticket.
71	    /// @param grossAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid, equal to `entryCount * ENTRY_PRICE`.
72	    event TicketPurchased(
73	        address indexed buyer,
74	        address indexed recipient,
75	        uint256 indexed ticketId,
76	        uint128 firstEntry,
77	        uint128 lastEntry,
78	        uint128 entryCount,
79	        uint256 grossAmount
80	    );
81	
82	    /// @notice Emitted when the raffle pays for and records its one Chainlink VRF request.
83	    /// @param requestId Wrapper-assigned request identifier.
84	    /// @param requester Address that initiated and funded the request.
85	    /// @param fee Native-token wei actually paid to the wrapper for the request.
86	    /// @param excessReturned Native-token wei returned to the requester after paying the actual fee.
87	    /// @param drawRequestedAt Unix timestamp, in seconds, when the request was accepted.
88	    /// @param callbackDeadline Exclusive Unix-timestamp deadline for accepting the authenticated callback.
89	    event DrawRequested(
90	        uint256 indexed requestId,
91	        address indexed requester,
92	        uint256 fee,
93	        uint256 excessReturned,
94	        uint256 drawRequestedAt,
95	        uint256 callbackDeadline
96	    );
97	
98	    /// @notice Emitted when an authenticated, ABI-decodable callback cannot resolve the raffle.
99	    /// @param receivedRequestId Request ID supplied by the wrapper callback.
100	    /// @param expectedRequestId Request ID currently recorded by the raffle, or zero before request persistence.
101	    /// @param status Current raffle status when the callback is ignored.
102	    event VrfCallbackIgnored(uint256 indexed receivedRequestId, uint256 indexed expectedRequestId, Status status);
103	
104	    /// @notice Emitted when an authenticated callback selects the winning entry and final result.
105	    /// @param requestId Request ID that produced the accepted randomness.
106	    /// @param winningEntry Selected one-based global entry number in `[1,totalEntries]`.
107	    /// @param result Final `NftWon` or `CashWon` result.
108	    event RaffleResolved(uint256 indexed requestId, uint128 indexed winningEntry, Status indexed result);
109	
110	    /// @notice Emitted when the raffle enters the full-refund branch.
111	    /// @param finalizer Address that enabled refunds.
112	    /// @param remainingRefundLiability Raw six-decimal quote-token units initially available for ticket refunds.
113	    event RefundsEnabled(address indexed finalizer, uint256 remainingRefundLiability);
114	
115	    /// @notice Emitted when the winning ticket is proven and all terminal quote-token liabilities are allocated.
116	    /// @param ticketId Ticket proven to contain the selected winning entry.
117	    /// @param settler Address that performed permissionless settlement.
118	    /// @param result Final `NftWon` or `CashWon` result.
119	    /// @param cashAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the cash winner; zero for `NftWon`.
120	    /// @param protocolFee Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the treasury, rounded down from gross sales.
121	    /// @param sponsorAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the sponsor recipient as the remainder.
122	    event WinningTicketSettled(
123	        uint256 indexed ticketId,
124	        address indexed settler,
125	        Status indexed result,
126	        uint256 cashAmount,
127	        uint256 protocolFee,
128	        uint256 sponsorAmount
129	    );
130	
131	    /// @notice Emitted when the winning ticket owner burns the ticket and receives the corresponding prize.
132	    /// @param ticketId Burned winning ticket ID.
133	    /// @param winner Ticket owner that received the prize at redemption time.
134	    /// @param result Final `NftWon` or `CashWon` result.
135	    /// @param cashAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid for `CashWon`; zero for `NftWon`.
136	    /// @param prizeToken ERC-721 prize contract for `NftWon`; the zero address for `CashWon`.
137	    /// @param prizeTokenId ERC-721 prize token ID for `NftWon`; zero for `CashWon`.
138	    event WinningTicketRedeemed(
139	        uint256 indexed ticketId,
140	        address indexed winner,
141	        Status indexed result,
142	        uint256 cashAmount,
143	        address prizeToken,
144	        uint256 prizeTokenId
145	    );
146	
147	    /// @notice Emitted when an owner burns one or more tickets for a full quote-token refund.
148	    /// @param owner Ticket owner that burned the tickets and received the refund.
149	    /// @param ticketQuantity Number of tickets burned in this transaction.
150	    /// @param entryQuantity Aggregate number of entries represented by the burned tickets.
151	    /// @param amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units refunded, equal to `entryQuantity * ENTRY_PRICE`.
152	    /// @param remainingRefundLiability Raw six-decimal quote-token units still claimable after this refund.
153	    event TicketsRefunded(
154	        address indexed owner,
155	        uint256 ticketQuantity,
156	        uint256 entryQuantity,
157	        uint256 amount,
158	        uint256 remainingRefundLiability
159	    );
160	
161	    /// @notice Emitted when the complete current sponsor balance is released to its immutable recipient.
162	    /// @param caller Address that triggered the permissionless release.
163	    /// @param recipient Immutable sponsor recipient that received the payment.
164	    /// @param amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid.
165	    event SponsorProceedsReleased(address indexed caller, address indexed recipient, uint256 amount);
166	
167	    /// @notice Emitted when the complete current protocol-fee balance is released to the immutable treasury.
168	    /// @param caller Address that triggered the permissionless release.
169	    /// @param treasury Immutable protocol treasury that received the payment.
170	    /// @param amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid.
171	    event ProtocolFeesReleased(address indexed caller, address indexed treasury, uint256 amount);
172	
173	    /// @notice Emitted when the escrowed prize is returned after a cash result or refund transition.
174	    /// @param caller Address that triggered the permissionless release.
175	    /// @param recipient Immutable sponsor recipient that received the prize.
176	    /// @param prizeToken ERC-721 contract of the returned prize.
177	    /// @param prizeTokenId Token ID of the returned prize.
178	    event SponsorPrizeReleased(
179	        address indexed caller, address indexed recipient, address indexed prizeToken, uint256 prizeTokenId
180	    );
181	
182	    // Errors
183	
184	    /// @notice Raised when a caller other than the immutable factory attempts clone initialization.
185	    error OnlyFactory();
186	
187	    /// @notice Raised when initialization is attempted more than once or on the locked implementation.
188	    error AlreadyInitialized();
189	
190	    /// @notice Raised when a required address is the zero address.
191	    error ZeroAddress();
192	
193	    /// @notice Raised when an operation is unavailable in the current lifecycle state.
194	    /// @param actual Current raffle status.
195	    error InvalidStatus(Status actual);
196	
197	    /// @notice Raised when an ERC-721 receiver callback does not exactly match the configured factory prize deposit.
198	    /// @param token ERC-721 contract that invoked the receiver callback.
199	    /// @param tokenId Token ID supplied by the callback.
200	    /// @param from Address identified as the previous token owner.
201	    /// @param operator Address identified as the transfer operator.
202	    error UnexpectedPrize(address token, uint256 tokenId, address from, address operator);
203	
204	    /// @notice Raised when an entry purchase is submitted at or after the exclusive sale end.
205	    /// @param endTime Exclusive sale-end Unix timestamp, in seconds.
206	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
207	    error SaleEnded(uint256 endTime, uint256 currentTime);
208	
209	    /// @notice Raised when an entry ticket would be minted to the zero address.
210	    error InvalidRecipient();
211	
212	    /// @notice Raised when a purchase requests no entries.
213	    error ZeroEntryCount();
214	
215	    /// @notice Raised when a purchase would exceed the `uint128` global entry-number representation.
216	    /// @param totalEntries Current global sold-entry count.
217	    /// @param requestedEntries Prospective entry count requested by the purchase.
218	    error TotalEntriesOverflow(uint128 totalEntries, uint128 requestedEntries);
219	
220	    /// @notice Raised when a refund batch is empty or exceeds the bounded ticket limit.
221	    /// @param quantity Number of supplied ticket IDs.
222	    /// @param maximum Maximum ticket IDs accepted per refund transaction.
223	    error InvalidTicketBatchSize(uint256 quantity, uint256 maximum);
224	
225	    /// @notice Raised when a quote-token claim targets a known protocol destination that could strand the claim.
226	    /// @param destination Rejected payout recipient.
227	    error InvalidQuoteDestination(address destination);
228	
229	    /// @notice Raised when a draw request is submitted before the sale end.
230	    /// @param endTime Exclusive sale-end Unix timestamp, in seconds.
231	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
232	    error RaffleNotEnded(uint256 endTime, uint256 currentTime);
233	
234	    /// @notice Raised when a draw request is submitted at or after the exclusive request deadline.
235	    /// @param deadline Exclusive draw-request Unix-timestamp deadline, in seconds.
236	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
237	    error DrawRequestWindowExpired(uint256 deadline, uint256 currentTime);
238	
239	    /// @notice Raised when draw initiation is attempted for a raffle with zero sold entries.
240	    error NoEntriesSold();
241	
242	    /// @notice Raised when refunds are requested before the applicable liveness deadline.
243	    /// @param deadline Unix timestamp, in seconds, at which refunds become available.
244	    /// @param currentTime Current block Unix timestamp, in seconds.
245	    error RefundsNotAvailable(uint256 deadline, uint256 currentTime);
246	
247	    /// @notice Raised when supplied native value cannot cover the quoted or actual Chainlink request fee.
248	    /// @param requiredFee Native-token wei required for the request.
249	    /// @param suppliedValue Native-token wei supplied by the caller.
250	    error InsufficientVrfFee(uint256 requiredFee, uint256 suppliedValue);
251	
252	    /// @notice Raised when excess native value cannot be returned to the draw requester.
253	    /// @param recipient Draw requester that was due the refund.
254	    /// @param amount Native-token wei that could not be returned.
255	    error NativeRefundFailed(address recipient, uint256 amount);
256	
257	    /// @notice Raised when no current cash-winner proceeds remain claimable.
258	    error NoWinnerProceeds();
259	
260	    /// @notice Raised when no current sponsor proceeds remain claimable.
261	    error NoSponsorProceeds();
262	
263	    /// @notice Raised when no current protocol fees remain claimable.
264	    error NoProtocolFees();
265	
266	    /// @notice Raised when initialization or a ticket transfer targets known protocol plumbing.
267	    /// @param destination Rejected address.
268	    error UnsafeProtocolDestination(address destination);
269	
270	    /// @notice Raised when the caller is not the current owner of the supplied ticket.
271	    /// @param ticketId Ticket whose ownership was checked.
272	    /// @param caller Address attempting the owner-only operation.
273	    /// @param owner Current ticket owner.
274	    error NotTicketOwner(uint256 ticketId, address caller, address owner);
275	
276	    /// @notice Raised when the supplied ticket range does not contain the selected winning entry.
277	    /// @param ticketId Supplied ticket ID.
278	    /// @param winningEntry Selected one-based global winning entry.
279	    error TicketDoesNotContainWinningEntry(uint256 ticketId, uint128 winningEntry);
280	
281	    /// @notice Raised when terminal liabilities have already been allocated.
282	    error SettlementAlreadyComplete();
283	
284	    /// @notice Raised when redemption supplies a ticket other than the recorded winning ticket.
285	    /// @param suppliedTicketId Ticket ID supplied for redemption.
286	    /// @param winningTicketId Previously settled winning ticket ID.
287	    error WinningTicketMismatch(uint256 suppliedTicketId, uint256 winningTicketId);
288	
289	    /// @notice Raised when the winning ticket has already been burned and redeemed.
290	    error WinningTicketAlreadyRedeemed();
291	
292	    /// @notice Raised when the sponsor prize cannot be returned in the current result state.
293	    /// @param status Current raffle status.
294	    error SponsorPrizeUnavailable(Status status);
295	
296	    /// @notice Raised when the escrowed prize has already been released.
297	    error PrizeAlreadyClaimed();
298	
299	    /// @notice Raised when the prize token does not report the expected owner after transfer.
300	    /// @param recipient Address that should own the prize after delivery.
301	    error PrizeDeliveryVerificationFailed(address recipient);
302	
303	    // External state-changing functions
304	
305	    /// @notice Initializes a fresh fixed-target clone with its immutable-per-raffle configuration.
306	    /// @dev Callable exactly once and only by the immutable canonical factory. Prize escrow activates the raffle later.
307	    /// @param params Clone-specific sponsor, prize, accounting, identifier, reserve, and timing configuration.
308	    function initialize(RaffleInitParams calldata params) external;
309	
310	    /// @notice Buys any positive number of entries and mints one sequential ticket containing their inclusive range.
311	    /// @param recipient Address that receives the newly minted ERC-721 range ticket.
312	    /// @param entryCount Prospective number of entries to buy for this ticket.
313	    /// @return ticketId Sequential ID of the newly minted ticket.
314	    function buyEntries(address recipient, uint128 entryCount) external returns (uint256 ticketId);
315	
316	    /// @notice Pays the current native Chainlink fee and requests the raffle's one random word.
317	    /// @dev Callable by anyone only in `[endTime,drawRequestDeadline())` after at least one entry is sold. Any native
318	    ///      value above the wrapper's actual fee is returned to the caller atomically.
319	    /// @return requestId Wrapper-assigned request identifier recorded by the raffle.
320	    function requestDraw() external payable returns (uint256 requestId);
321	
322	    /// @notice Enables full refunds after the sold-raffle request deadline or an accepted request's callback deadline.
323	    ///         Also closes an empty raffle immediately for the sponsor and after sale end for anyone.
324	    function enableRefunds() external;
325	
326	    /// @notice Proves which ticket contains the winning entry and allocates winner, sponsor, and protocol liabilities.
327	    /// @dev Anyone may execute; ownership is not read, the ticket remains transferable, and no external asset transfer
328	    ///      occurs. The cash-winner allocation is rounded down; the sponsor receives the remaining raw units.
329	    /// @param ticketId Ticket whose stored inclusive range must contain `winningEntry`.
330	    /// @return cashAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units allocated to the winner, or zero for an NFT result.
331	    function settleWinningTicket(uint256 ticketId) external returns (uint256 cashAmount);
332	
333	    /// @notice Lets the current winning-ticket owner atomically burn the ticket and receive the NFT or cash prize.
334	    /// @dev If necessary, this first settles the supplied winning ticket so the owner can complete both steps in one
335	    ///      transaction. Any failed delivery reverts the burn and every redemption state change.
336	    /// @param ticketId Winning ticket to settle if needed, burn, and redeem.
337	    /// @return cashAmount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid for `CashWon`, or zero for `NftWon`.
338	    function redeemWinningTicket(uint256 ticketId) external returns (uint256 cashAmount);
339	
340	    /// @notice Burns an owner-selected batch of tickets and returns their full entry purchase value.
341	    /// @dev Accepts one to 100 tickets. Duplicate, nonexistent, or foreign-owned IDs revert the entire batch.
342	    /// @param ticketIds Ticket IDs owned by the caller and submitted for refund.
343	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid, equal to represented entries times `ENTRY_PRICE`.
344	    function refundTickets(uint256[] calldata ticketIds) external returns (uint256 amount);
345	
346	    /// @notice Releases the complete current sponsor-proceeds balance to the immutable sponsor recipient.
347	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid in this release.
348	    function releaseSponsorProceeds() external returns (uint256 amount);
349	
350	    /// @notice Releases the complete current protocol-fee balance to the immutable treasury.
351	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units paid in this release.
352	    function releaseProtocolFees() external returns (uint256 amount);
353	
354	    /// @notice Returns the escrowed prize to the immutable sponsor recipient after `CashWon` or `Refunding`.
355	    function releaseSponsorPrize() external;
356	
357	    // External view functions
358	
359	    /// @notice Returns the wrapper's current native direct-funding price for the configured callback.
360	    /// @return fee Native-token wei currently quoted by the wrapper; the value may change before request inclusion.
361	    function getVrfRequestPrice() external view returns (uint256 fee);
362	
363	    /// @notice Estimates the native direct-funding price at a caller-selected gas price.
364	    /// @param requestGasPriceWei Prospective transaction gas price in wei per gas.
365	    /// @return fee Estimated native-token wei for the configured callback and one random word.
366	    function estimateVrfRequestPrice(uint256 requestGasPriceWei) external view returns (uint256 fee);
367	
368	    /// @notice Returns the inclusive global entry range represented by a ticket ID.
369	    /// @dev Returns zeros for an ID that has never been minted; ranges remain historical after ticket burns.
370	    /// @param ticketId Sequential ticket ID to inspect.
371	    /// @return firstEntry First represented one-based global entry, inclusive.
372	    /// @return lastEntry Last represented one-based global entry, inclusive.
373	    function ticketRange(uint256 ticketId) external view returns (uint128 firstEntry, uint128 lastEntry);
374	
375	    /// @notice Returns the exclusive deadline for initiating the draw.
376	    /// @return deadline Unix timestamp, in seconds, equal to `endTime + 2 days`.
377	    function drawRequestDeadline() external view returns (uint256 deadline);
378	
379	    /// @notice Returns the exclusive deadline for accepting the authenticated callback.
380	    /// @return deadline Unix timestamp, in seconds, equal to `drawRequestedAt + 2 days`, or zero before a request.
381	    function callbackDeadline() external view returns (uint256 deadline);
382	
383	    /// @notice Returns all currently outstanding quote-token liabilities tracked by the raffle.
384	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units across the unsettled pot, refunds, and allocated claims.
385	    function accountedQuoteBalance() external view returns (uint256 amount);
386	
387	    /// @notice Returns lifetime gross sales derived from the global sold-entry count.
388	    /// @dev No redundant gross-sales value is stored.
389	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units equal to `totalEntries * ENTRY_PRICE`.
390	    function grossSales() external view returns (uint256 amount);
391	
392	    // Public generated getters
393	
394	    /// @notice Returns the fixed raw six-decimal quote-token price of one entry.
395	    /// @return price One entry price, exactly 1,000,000 raw units.
396	    function ENTRY_PRICE() external view returns (uint256 price);
397	
398	    /// @notice Returns the fixed Chainlink callback execution limit.
399	    /// @return gasLimit Callback gas units requested from the wrapper.
400	    function callbackGasLimit() external view returns (uint32 gasLimit);
401	
402	    /// @notice Returns the fixed Chainlink confirmation count.
403	    /// @return confirmations Blocks requested before callback fulfillment.
404	    function requestConfirmations() external view returns (uint16 confirmations);
405	
406	    /// @notice Returns the immutable factory authorized to initialize this implementation's clones.
407	    /// @return factoryAddress Canonical factory address.
408	    function factory() external view returns (address factoryAddress);
409	
410	    /// @notice Returns the prize depositor and pre-end empty-raffle refund authority.
411	    /// @return sponsorAddress Immutable-per-raffle sponsor address.
412	    function sponsor() external view returns (address sponsorAddress);
413	
414	    /// @notice Returns the immutable recipient of sponsor quote proceeds and returned prizes.
415	    /// @return recipient Sponsor recipient address.
416	    function sponsorRecipient() external view returns (address recipient);
417	
418	    /// @notice Returns the immutable recipient of this raffle's protocol fees.
419	    /// @return treasury Protocol treasury address.

421	
422	    /// @notice Returns the immutable canonical six-decimal USDC contract.
423	    /// @return token Canonical USDC contract trusted by this factory deployment.
424	    function quoteToken() external view returns (IERC20 token);
425

427	    /// @return wrapper Wrapper contract.

429	
430	    /// @notice Returns the configured ERC-721 prize contract.
431	    /// @return token Prize-token contract.

433	
434	    /// @notice Returns the configured ERC-721 prize token ID.
435	    /// @return tokenId Escrowed prize token ID.
436	    function prizeTokenId() external view returns (uint256 tokenId);
437	
438	    /// @notice Returns this raffle's one-based canonical factory identifier.
439	    /// @return id Raffle identifier.
440	    function raffleId() external view returns (uint256 id);
441	
442	    /// @notice Returns the global entry threshold that selects the NFT outcome when met or exceeded.
443	    /// @return entries Reserve entry count.
444	    function reserveEntries() external view returns (uint128 entries);
445	
446	    /// @notice Returns the exclusive sale-end timestamp.
447	    /// @return timestamp Unix timestamp, in seconds.
448	    function endTime() external view returns (uint64 timestamp);
449	
450	    /// @notice Returns the lifetime global number of entries sold.
451	    /// @return entries Sold-entry count; also the last assigned global entry number.
452	    function totalEntries() external view returns (uint128 entries);
453	
454	    /// @notice Returns the lifetime number of range tickets minted.
455	    /// @return tickets Ticket count; also the latest assigned ticket ID.

465	
466	    /// @notice Returns the address that burned and redeemed the winning ticket.

472	    function winnerProceeds() external view returns (uint256 amount);

476	    function sponsorProceeds() external view returns (uint256 amount);
477	
478	    /// @notice Returns the current protocol-fee liability.
479	    /// @return amount Raw six-decimal quote-token units claimable by the immutable treasury.
480	    function protocolFees() external view returns (uint256 amount);
481

483	    /// @return requestId Wrapper-assigned ID, or zero before request persistence.
484	    function vrfRequestId() external view returns (uint256 requestId);

487	    /// @return timestamp Unix timestamp, in seconds, or zero before request persistence.
488	    function drawRequestedAt() external view returns (uint64 timestamp);
489

492	    function resolvedAt() external view returns (uint64 timestamp);
493	
494	    /// @notice Returns the selected one-based global winning entry.
495	    /// @return entry Entry in `[1,totalEntries]`, or zero before resolution.
496	    function winningEntry() external view returns (uint128 entry);
497

504	    function status() external view returns (Status currentStatus);
505

507	    /// @return complete True after winning-ticket settlement.
508	    function settlementComplete() external view returns (bool complete);

518	    /// @notice Returns whether this implementation or clone has completed its one-time initialization step.
519	    /// @return complete True for the locked implementation and every initialized clone.
520	    function initialized() external view returns (bool complete);
